edit.description: `committed_layout_sites` (:54) collects discovered committed members of LAYOUT-content kinds only (the `Content::Layout` filter at :67, the `commitment != Local` exclusion at :68), so 676467cf's undeclared-member finding never sees a composed kind. Generalize it to one site walk over every discovered kind, tagging each site with its content class. ONE predicate, spelled once: `content == Content::File && governs.is_some() && commitment != Local`. Each conjunct is load-bearing — the `local` exclusion is already there, `governs == None` drops a nested-file child (it composes its path from its host and holds no rollup row), and the content class drops the four registration kinds. Those four (hook, installed-plugin, known-marketplace, mcp-server) fall out on the content test ALONE: each is `Content::Fields` carrying a `collection_address` (src/builtin_kind.rs:347, :378, :418, :462), its lock residue `[[declaration.registration]]` and never a provenance row, so joining them would forge false findings over the gauntlet and move the snapshot this entry forbids moving. Do NOT add a `collection_address.is_none()` exclusion beside the content test: the two are not the same predicate (a `Content::Fields` kind with no collection address passes one and fails the other), and a second spelling of one rule is the disease. If a `Content::File` kind carrying a `collection_address` proves admissible, keep it excluded and say why in the commit body rather than widening the predicate silently. Keep the layout branch's rule id and message byte-identical so tests/layout_kind.rs stays green untouched. Gate the whole check on lock presence — on an unrepresented harness every discovered member is undeclared and the finding must stay silent; the layout branch inherits that gate too (it is vacuously safe there today, since layout kinds exist only via lock rows, but it is genuinely load-bearing for file-locus built-ins). Unlike the guard (GUARD-UNDECLARED-LOCUS-WRITE excludes a `.`-rooted locus for want of an ignore reader), `check` KEEPS `.`-rooted loci — `memory` governs `.` with `**/CLAUDE.md` — on purpose: discovery already prunes by the repo's ignore rules (src/import.rs:321-335), so the walk judged is the walk made. Name that deliberate divergence in the commit body. Thread the undeclared set into `coverage_note::check` (:544) — which means MOVING the site walk above that call, from its current home at :563-570.

Beside `undeclared_layout_members_from_doc` (:2820): the composed-kind counterpart. A composed member's whole trace on the lock is its projection provenance row, not the five `MEMBER_ADDRESS_COLUMNS` (:2764) declaration families a layout host reaches through — so this one joins each discovered site's `source_path` against `read_prior_provenance_from_doc` (:2272), the same rows `emit_owned_targets` (:3268) and `config_stale` (:2713) already walk. Normalize BOTH sides through `normalize_lock_path` (:806) before comparing, exactly as the emit reap-diff does at :1417: the site's path is a `String` from `path::relativize_against_root` (gate.rs:74-77) while `ProvenanceRow.source_path` (:2240) is a `HarnessRelativePath`, and an older lock's `./x` spelling would otherwise forge a finding. A discovered document at a represented kind's locus that no provenance row names is reported `locus.undeclared-member` at `warn`, naming path and kind: `emit` will never maintain it (orphan classification iterates lock rows at :1416, so a disk file with no row is never classified and no orphan-drift is reported over it) and `guard` never bound it, yet Claude Code loads it. Remedy named first is declare the member and re-emit. The `local` remedy is offered only for a CUSTOM kind — a built-in cannot be re-declared until BUILTIN-KIND-RELOCATION-EDGE-FIELDS lands. That the sibling layout message at :2832 offers `local` unconditionally is deliberate, not an inconsistency to fix here: no built-in kind carries `Content::Layout` (it arrives only from a lock row), so every layout kind is one whose commitment the author can respell. Say that in the commit body; tests/layout_kind.rs:715's `local` assertion does not move. RIDER (comment staleness, this file's next opener carries it): `ClauseRow::field`'s doc comment at :3562 still reads "The field (or marker) the predicate constrains, when it names one", which 767f4941 outgrew — `section_contains` and `require_sections` name no field and now carry a SYNTHESIZED `<heading>.<marker>` label from `clauseField` (sdk/src/declarations.ts:171). Reword it as the clause's compiled label, the term `specs/model/pipeline.md` ("The lock") uses.

`check` (:57) renders `coverage.checked` (:28) from `member_counts` alone, so a stranger document at a governed locus inflates a kind's count with no mark — the observed 11 -> 13. Take the undeclared set gate.rs now computes and disclose declared and undeclared apart per kind, so the one line that says what was checked cannot silently absorb a member the program does not declare. Hard constraint: the line stays BYTE-IDENTICAL when a kind has zero undeclared members — `tests/snapshots/gauntlet__check_diagnostics.snap:7` pins the whole rendering and `tests/gate_fail_loud.rs:228` asserts the `skill (1)` substring (that fixture writes no lock, so the lock-presence gate keeps it green regardless), so the undeclared mark appends only where there is one.

The fixtures here already build harness dirs with a committed lock and read findings back off the GitHub reporter's one-line-per-finding form (`write_skill`, `lock_widget_kind`, `check_harness`), which is exactly this entry's shape. Three new regressions per tests[], plus TWO existing arms that gain an undeclared mark because their own fixtures carry an undeclared document: `an_embedded_kind_with_nested_members_renders_a_nonzero_embedded_marked_count` (:378), whose `assert!(summary.contains("skill (1)"))` at :410 fails once the summary gains the mark, and `a_locked_custom_kind_suppresses_the_surface_it_governs` (:335), which gains an advisory finding its existing assertions survive but which must be pinned rather than left implicit.

`coverage_note::check` is called directly here at :388 with five arguments; threading the undeclared set through it is a compile error in this file until the call is updated. No behavioural claim of this suite changes — it pins cost, not findings.

The gauntlet corpus's whole `coverage.checked` rendering is pinned here (:7). Its members are all declared, so the disclosure change must leave this snapshot unmoved — it is in the fence so a genuine, justified move can be accepted rather than reverting the tick on the fence, not as licence to reformat the line.

summary: A document dropped at a represented kind's locus that the lock declares no member for is admitted, counted, and never named — the file-locus half of 676467cf.

tests.asserts: an undeclared `.claude/rules/*.md` in a represented harness yields one `locus.undeclared-member` warn naming its path and kind, and the `coverage.checked` disclosure counts it apart from the declared members of that kind

the same harness with that document declared and emitted reports neither the finding nor an undeclared count — and asserts a non-zero declared count first, so the silence is not an empty read (0048's conservation bar)
an unrepresented harness (no lock) checked under the built-in default contract reports no `locus.undeclared-member` at all, however many documents discovery finds

acceptance: Invariant 6's "no read or lowering represents less than it was given" holds for a discovered document with no declared member: `check` names it, the disclosure counts it apart, and neither fires on an unrepresented harness or on a declared-and-emitted one. 676467cf's `layout.undeclared-member` keeps its rule id and wording — tests/layout_kind.rs is untouched and green. The `coverage.checked` rendering is unchanged wherever no kind has an undeclared member — `tests/snapshots/gauntlet__check_diagnostics.snap` does not move, which the registration kinds' `Content::Fields` class is what buys. Stated consequence, not an accident: `locus.undeclared-member` is `warn`, and `--deny-advisories` (src/main.rs:256-259) promotes every `Warn` while exempting `Note`, so from this entry on CI fails for any represented harness carrying an undeclared document at a governed locus. That is the teeth; it is also what an adopter meets first. Seventeen test files write both a lock and a surface document, so read the run rather than the diff: none asserts an exact binary-driven finding count today (the count assertions in tests/ are library-level or rule-filtered), but a `--no-fail-fast` run is what proves it. `cargo test --no-fail-fast` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` green.

edit.description: `guard` (:840) allows outright any path not equal to a lock-declared emit-owned target (the `matches_projection` gate at :850-853) — so creating `.claude/rules/stray.md` in a REPRESENTED harness passes, while the no-lock fallback (:858, `is_claude_path` at :886) would have bound the very same write. Representation currently loosens the boundary. Bind a write whose path falls inside a represented committed kind's `governs` locus but matches no emit-owned target: the program declares no member there, `emit` will never maintain the file, and Claude Code loads it anyway. Judged through the existing `GuardVerdict`/enforcement-mode path, never escalated past the declared mode; the message names the kind whose locus it landed in and the declare-and-re-emit remedy CHECK-UNDECLARED-MEMBER-AT-A-GOVERNED-LOCUS's finding names. The locus test is the kind's `root` joined to its `glob`, compiled through `glob::compile_glob` (src/glob.rs:19, `literal_separator(true)`) with `import::scan_locus`'s segment semantics (src/import.rs:341) — NOT `CustomKind::owns_source` (src/kind.rs:725), which matches the glob's leaf against a bare filename (`rule`'s `*.md` would match any markdown anywhere) and cannot serve as a locus test at all. Two loci are excluded by construction: a `local`-commitment one (its documents are the author's own by declaration — `settings-local` at `.claude/settings.local.json` and `dial` at `.temper/dial.toml`, per representation.md's "a local member is read-side only ... never an emit input or target"), and a `.`-rooted one (`memory` governs `.` with `**/CLAUDE.md`; the guard has no ignore reader where discovery prunes by the repo's ignore rules at src/import.rs:321-335, so binding it would judge every CLAUDE.md in the tree, vendored ones included, and disagree with `check`). Name the `memory` gap in the commit body rather than closing it with a walk the guard cannot afford.

`Command::Guard` (:332) already reads `declarations` (:346), `lock_present` (:348) and `emit_owned_targets` (:349) before the stdin read. Hand `install::guard` the represented committed kinds' loci — but source them the way `guarded_manifests` (:556-602) already sources the manifest set twelve lines below, NOT off `declarations.kinds`: a `[[declaration.kind]]` row exists only for a kind the program actually uses, so the gauntlet lock carries no `agent` row and cascade's carries none either, and sourcing from lock rows leaves `.claude/agents/stray.md` allowed — the entry would not close the issue it was cut from, and the guard would disagree with the check side, which walks `overlaid_builtin_kinds` and covers every built-in. So: `builtin_kind::definitions()` overlaid through `compose::overlay_builtin_kind`, plus `compose::partition_kind_rows`'s custom rows, filtered by `commitment != local`, `governs.is_some()`, `collection_address.is_none()` (the manifest kinds stay `manifest_write_findings`'s) and a non-`.` root. That is pure embedded data, no disk read and no walk — the guard runs on every tool call, so the cost bound is the existing one. State in the commit body that this reads loci from embedded kind data rather than lock rows, against distribution.md's "Placements are lock-grounded, never assumed": `guarded_manifests` already makes exactly that call, and the alternative silently under-binds every kind the program has no member of yet.

Regressions beside the existing guard cases, per tests[] — and ONE existing assertion this entry inverts: :1364 asserts "an undeclared .claude/ path is allowed when targets exist" for a write to `.claude/skills/x/SKILL.md`, which is precisely the hole being closed; rewrite it to the new verdict rather than leaving it to fail. Pin the arms that genuinely do not move: a write to a declared projection keeps its current verdict verbatim, `.claude/settings.json` keeps the manifest arm's verdict (it reaches `install::guard` whenever `manifest_write_findings` returns `None`, as it does for a `PendingManifest::Unrecognized` payload at :1165 — without the `collection_address` exclusion the new binding would catch it and change that verdict), a write to a `local`-commitment locus is never bound, and the no-lock `.claude/` fallback is untouched.

The other guard-driving suite: `common::run_guard` cases at :500, :511, :531, :557, :573 and :588 cover the block/warn/note modes, the README.md-is-allowed arm, the unreadable-lock arms and the no-lock fallback. None should move — README.md sits in no governed locus, and `memory`'s `.`-rooted one is excluded — but this file is where a mis-scoped locus set shows up first, so run it and pin whatever the new binding touches rather than discovering it at the merge.

summary: In a represented harness the guard allows any write outside the lock's exact projection paths — including creating an undeclared document inside a governed locus.

per.section: The placements and their enforcement modes

tests.asserts: block mode denies (exit 2) a Write creating an undeclared `.claude/rules/*.md` in a represented harness, naming the `rule` kind whose locus it landed in; warn surfaces in-band and allows; note allows silently

a write to a lock-declared projection keeps its existing verdict, a write to a `local`-commitment locus is never bound BY THE NEW LOCUS BINDING, and an unrepresented harness keeps the `.claude/` fallback unchanged — which still binds `.claude/settings.local.json` at the declared mode, since `is_claude_path` (src/install.rs:886) is a substring match on `.claude/`; 'never bound' holds only under a lock

acceptance: The guard's binding no longer depends on a path being an exact lock row: a write into a represented committed kind's locus that declares no member there is judged at the author's declared enforcement mode, so a represented harness is at least as protected as an unrepresented one — including `.claude/agents/`, which a lock-row-sourced locus set would have missed. Exactly one existing arm inverts (tests/install.rs:1364) and it inverts deliberately; the declared-projection, represented-manifest, local-locus and no-lock-fallback arms each report the verdict they do today. SCOPE, stated because it is the largest behavior change the first adopter meets and it must not arrive as a surprise: the binding is every non-`.`-rooted governed locus of a represented committed kind, NOT `.claude/` — the entry's examples are `.claude/` only because this harness is. On cascade's own harness (block mode) that set includes specs/intent, specs/domain, specs/features and specs/surfaces, so a hand `Write` creating specs/intent/north-star.md exits 2 the day this lands. That is correct under cascade's own law — its specs are projections emitted through Bash, which the guard does not instrument — and it is the hole being closed, but it ships as a stated consequence. `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` green.

edit.description: read_collection_member (222) takes a LayoutMember's leaves from its immediate sub-headings only, keyed by slug; the paragraph directly under the member's own heading lands nowhere. Land it under whichever reserved leaf key `(layout-own-span-leaf)` rules — composed leaves are author-named (NestedMemberRow.leaves keyed by field name, no reserved own-span key exists there; the SDK's `FRAMEWORK_KEYS`/kind.ts:245 `prose` is a member-level value, not a leaf-name reservation). Hazards the fork must rule on: node.body includes sub-heading text (the own span must cut at the first child heading), and a sub-heading slugged to the reserved name would collide with it.
Regression: a layout collection member whose body is `### Title` + a paragraph + `**Test.** ...` (no sub-headings) materializes a non-empty leaves map carrying the paragraph under the ruled key.

FRAMEWORK_KEYS (~245) reserves `prose` as a member-level value only; once `(layout-own-span-leaf)` rules a reserved own-span leaf key, an author's sub-heading slugging to that same name needs a collision guard (or explicit precedence rule) — the exact key and whether it joins FRAMEWORK_KEYS stays whatever the fork rules, not invented here.

edit.description: Add `relocate(base, delta)` beside the existing `kind()` factory (~431 — shifted from ~336 by f8ba355b's discriminated-union narrowing, verified on disk 09-07). KindFacts is now three inlined object-literal union branches, one per locus shape (~168-310), each already near-fully duplicated by design (that commit's own rationale: no intermediate named types requiring root-level exports). A spread-merge (`{...base, edgeFields: delta.edgeFields}`) should stay within whichever branch `base` already is and type-check as KindFacts without touching all three by hand — confirm this holds under real tsc rather than assuming, since a marker field no branch currently declares (e.g. `facts.relocates`) is exactly the case a discriminated union complicates; if it doesn't type-check cleanly, a side-channel marker (outside KindFacts) is the fallback, not a third duplication of the union. Mark the produced facts with a relocation marker (e.g. `facts.relocates`) so KINDS-IN-PLAY-NAME-COLLISION-REFUSAL can later tell a legitimate relocation from a genuine name collision.
SDK-side payload assertion: a relocated `rule` kind declaring an added edgeField emits the fact in its compiled declarations (no `as any`, no dropped field).

Rust regression: the emitted edge fact from a relocated built-in resolves a real graph.route edge — proving no engine change is needed, since edges are always read from assembly `edge` rows keyed by `from` kind (never carried on a kind row itself); `graph.route` isn't assertable from an SDK test, hence the split.

This file already carries the corpus's one existing relocation vocabulary — a lock-row `row_relocates_builtin` (src/compose.rs:1091) recognizes a same-named row as a legitimate built-in relocation purely structurally (format/unit_shape/registration compatible), with no marker field at all, and doesn't examine edgeFields either — so a corpus kind named `rule` with an added edgeField should already flow through that existing Rust-side path with no engine change (matching this entry's own claim). Before minting a new `facts.relocates` marker in the SDK, confirm it doesn't duplicate `row_relocates_builtin`'s concept under a second name; if the marker is genuinely SDK-layer-only (needed before compilation to a KindFactRow), name that distinction explicitly rather than leaving two same-purpose 'relocates' vocabularies unreconciled. Extend this file's relocated-built-in fixtures if a new end-to-end case is the cleanest proof.

`row_relocates_builtin` is DEFINED here (:1091) and read at :460/:1114 — the corpus's one existing 'relocates' vocabulary. Where the entry concludes the SDK-side `facts.relocates` marker is a distinct, SDK-layer-only concept, that distinction is named at this definition's doc comment so the two vocabularies are reconciled in the same diff, not left as two same-purpose names. Behaviour unchanged: overlay_builtin_kind (:453) never carries edgeFields. Read-only mentions at src/kind.rs:94, src/admissibility.rs:123/426 and tests/lock_declaration_rows.rs:1878 are prose that rides the next entry opening those files (standing prose-cite rule), not this fence.

summary: A built-in kind cannot take an added edge field; the SDK has no sanctioned relocation constructor and an as any cast drops the edge fact silently.

tests.asserts: a relocated built-in kind's added edge field is emitted, not silently dropped by an as any cast

acceptance: A corpus can add an edge field to a built-in kind (e.g. rule) via the sanctioned relocation form and have it resolve a real graph edge, checked at check and rendered at emit — no as any cast needed. No engine change required: overlay_builtin_kind (compose.rs:453) never needs to carry edgeFields, since edges never live on a kind row. Per 0048's conservation bar, the regression pins non-vacuity: it asserts the relocated kind's edge fact is actually present (non-empty) in the compiled declarations before checking it resolves a real edge.

edit.description: `narrate_kind` (:534, binding the `KindFactRow` at :544 and holding the whole `kind_facts` slice at :537) renders three strands — guidance and cite, layout regions plus skeleton, hosted kinds — and nothing else (:534-582), so a kind whose row declares only guidance prints one line and stops. Three more strands, all renderable off data already in hand, no signature change: (i) the **locus** — and it is NOT either/or: `hook` carries `governs_root = ".claude"`, `governs_glob = "settings.json"` AND `collection_address = { manifest, key_path }`, so render the collection address (in src/drift.rs: the `KindFactRow` column at :3440, its `manifest`/`key_path` fields at :3479/:3482) as where the MEMBER keys and `governs_root`/`governs_glob` (:3390/:3394) as where the host document is discovered, plus the `registration` channel labels (:3417 — the wire spelling is the call form the SDK writes, `event(event)` for `hook`, per sdk/src/declarations.ts:219-234 and .temper/lock.toml:72) and the `commitment` class (:3405), which is part of where a member lands (a local kind's members are uncommitted); a file-locus kind shows the governs line alone. (ii) the **hosting kinds** inverse — which kinds host members of this one — restored, not dropped: it is the prerequisite for (iii), because the row cannot say whether a member is top-level or embedded (`orientation` is embedded yet its row carries `unit_shape = "file"` and no `governs`), and the oracle is a scan over the other `kind_facts` rows' path-less `templates` entries and `content.regions[].member_kind` for this kind's name. (iii) the **address form** — `<kind>:<name>` for a top-level kind, `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>` for one only ever hosted, EMBEDDED VALUE OR FILE CHILD ALIKE: a nested-file child is a `[[declaration.nested_member]]` row carrying `host = "skill:test-skill"` (tests/coverage_note.rs:391-396), so `supporting-doc` takes the host-qualified form exactly as an embedded value does. Which means strand (ii)'s oracle must scan path-BEARING `templates` entries too, not only path-less ones, or a file-child kind's hosts go unnamed and (iii) has nothing to read — read from the single address-grammar home MEMBER-ADDRESS-GRAMMAR-ONE-HOME establishes (`src/member_address.rs`), never a second hand-spelling. Two mechanics: the early return at :554-567 ("nothing to teach") fires when guidance, cite, layout, embedded and file-children are all absent, so it must gain the locus and hosting terms or the new strands never print; and the address form must ride that same guard rather than rendering unconditionally off the kind name, or `explain_narrates_a_kind_absent_guidance_cleanly` (tests/read_verbs.rs:1065, which passes `&[]` rows) goes red. Reword that line from "nothing to teach before a member of it exists" to naming the strands. All of this must render with ZERO members of the kind in the corpus — the adopter's actual moment, and the reason this is not `corpus_leaves` (:817), which can only report what existing members carry.

Regressions on a MEMBER-LESS surface, per tests[] — the non-vacuity bar is that the fixture carries zero members of the explained kind, so the lines cannot be coming from a corpus read. `explain_kind` (:819) is the helper both new tests use; it synthesizes contracts from the rows, so a kind is only resolvable if it has a row. Keep the existing arm at :1065 where a kind with no row at all still prints its clean "nothing declared" line rather than falling silent. It is NOT byte-for-byte: it asserts `contains("No authoring guidance is declared")` (:1101) and the absence of a `‣` marker (:1105), so the reword must keep that opening clause and may change only the tail after the em dash — and the address form must ride the same guard, or the arm goes red on the marker-free line growing an address it has no row to source. No snapshot moves: nothing under tests/snapshots/ asserts explain-kind output, and the CLI-driven `explain_in` calls in tests/layout_kind.rs and tests/lock_declaration_rows.rs all target members, not kinds.

VERIFY-ONLY — expect no diff. The `kind_facts(name, governs_root, governs_glob)` builder (:614-631) always sets BOTH governs fields, so every existing bare-kind test that builds a row gains a locus line: tests/read_verbs.rs:763, :915, :970, :1015. All four assert with `contains`, so they stay green while their output grows. In the fence so the builder can gain a no-locus variant if a new arm needs one, not because an edit is expected.

summary: `explain kind:<x>` never says where a member of the kind lands or how a reference to one is spelled — the two lines an adopter with no member yet most needs.

tests.asserts: `explain kind:hook` on a surface with zero hook members names its `hooks.<Event>` collection address, the `.claude/settings.json` document its members are discovered in, its `event(event)` registration channel label, and the address form a reference to one of its members takes

`explain kind:rule` on a surface with zero rule members names its file locus and its `kind:name` address form; a kind hosted only by another names the `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>` form and the kinds that host it; and a kind with no row at all still prints the "nothing declared" line unchanged

acceptance: On a surface carrying no member of the kind, `explain kind:<name>` prints where a member of it lands and how a reference to one is spelled, alongside the guidance, layout and hosted-kind strands 3dcc73f1 already renders — the read verb narrating a kind, not only a kind that already has members. `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` green.
notes: Routed from inbox 09-07 (cascade on GH #47, observed at ab61fea4). edit.description: Thirteen live address-producing lines here, not the nine this entry first counted: the member table's top-level keys (:771, :775), the nested table's qualified (:798) and bare (:799-800) spellings, `resolvedTargetFacts`'s returned address (:353), the placement keys (:515, :555), the host on payload members (:815), and the three diagnostic-prose spellings (:181, :208, :341) — which render an address into a message and take the same writer, so a refusal quotes the spelling the resolver actually looked up. Plus the bare-form LIFT at :295 (`edge.to.length === 1 && !address.includes(":") ? `${edge.to[0]}:${address}` : address`), the direct counterpart of Rust `target_identity`'s single-element prefix strip (src/graph.rs:1609-1614), and its verbatim restatement in the comment at :294 — both matched by this entry's own acceptance regex, so both move or the acceptance stays red. Design bar on that one: the bare `kind:key` spelling is what 0049 lists under Rejected ("Corpus-unique keys as the address ... Uniqueness is the resolver's bar, not the grammar's"), so expose it as a LOOKUP KEY, never as an address writer — the two ends already agree (Rust strips the prefix back off before matching) and a builder must not "fix" the apparent mismatch.

Seven sites, every cite 26 higher than this entry first spelled them: the host address at :480, :502, :570, :725 and :869, the qualified nested address at :873, and the leaf address at :534 — whose own doc comment (the block at :523-531, the cross-seam cite at :529) points at `src/read.rs`'s `parse_leaf_address` as the grammar it must match, the cite that goes stale the moment either side moves. That cite is re-pointed at the new module here, discharging the stale-prose exception MEMBER-ADDRESS-GRAMMAR-ONE-HOME's acceptance parks on this file.

`mentionOf` (:29) spells `${member.kind}:${member.name}` — its doc comment (:24-26) calls it "the convention every corpus repeats to cite a member from prose, captured once here", which is true of this function and false of the module: it is one of twenty-one producers across three files. Read the writer.

VERIFY-ONLY — expect no diff, and the file this entry's "byte-identical" claim actually rides on: :320's case pins the ambiguous-bare-key refusal and :361 asserts its wording byte-for-byte (`/a bare key 2 hosts carry \(`rule:rust`, `rule:sdk`\)/`). Routing emit.ts:341's prose spelling through a writer must leave that string untouched. In the fence so a forced wording change can land visibly rather than as a surprise red.

unchanged and green — the extraction is behaviour-preserving, so the existing edge-resolution and member-table suites are the non-vacuity pin

edit.description: `local_document_rows` (:851) calls `read_layout_document`, which already returns the captured spans on `LayoutDocumentRows.prose` (src/drift.rs:1955), and then extends only `rows.nested` and `rows.satisfies` (:883-884) — the prose is read and dropped. Carry it: extend `rows.prose` too, and in `assemble_lock_family` (:1054-1055) collect the local kinds' prose rows into a new `local_layout_prose: Vec<drift::LayoutProseRow>` field on `LockFamily` (:405), beside `local_members` (:424) and for the same stated reason — the documents are uncommitted, so no consumer below can find them again short of a second walk that could disagree with this read. It does NOT go on `drift::Declarations` (:3331): that is the SDK→engine seam payload with a generated TS twin, and `layout_prose` is emit-derived output the seam has never carried.

`explain_target` destructures `LockFamily` at :2038 (taking `declarations` and `overlaid_builtin_kinds`) and its prose strand reads `drift::layout_prose_from_doc(&lock_doc)` at :2189 — the committed rows only. Take `local_layout_prose` off the same destructure and union it with the lock-document rows before `prose_strand` (:1989), so one narration covers both faces. Update the strand's sited comment above :2185, which today says the rows are 'a lock row keyed by the host's address' — true of the committed half only once local rows join it.

Regression: a local-locus layout kind whose document carries a preamble under a verbatim prose region — `explain <kind>:<id>` narrates the captured span, the same strand a committed layout member gets. Pins the read-time half of f07d4f84, which shipped the committed half and named this one as unwired.

summary: A local-locus layout member's captured prose is read and dropped at read time, so `explain` narrates nothing where the committed half now narrates the span.

tests.asserts: `explain` on a local-locus layout member narrates its captured prose region, matching the committed half's strand

acceptance: `cargo test` green with the local_locus regression. A local-locus layout member's verbatim prose region reaches a read-time row and `explain`'s prose strand, so no layout document's authored span is read and dropped on either face (invariant 6). Non-vacuity per 0048's bar: the regression asserts the narrated span carries the document's actual preamble text, never merely that a strand appeared.
